mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 0.5% indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when GDPC1 falls by more than 0.5% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals labor market overheating, which historically precedes Fed tightening and higher input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 4% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.5% signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both fall > 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and HOUST decline by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate above 2% with simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% signals a policy shift toward rate cuts in the near future, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps > 0.5% in one month AND CPIAUCSL < 1.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL falls below 1.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 2% for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which historically precedes consumer spending pullbacks and negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS rises above 2% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) is a statistical artifact but may indicate labor market data inconsistency; however, if observed, it signals confusion in labor market signals, leading to elevated market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 500K units for six consecutive months signals a prolonged housing downturn, which reduces construction-related earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST remains below 500K for six consecutive months.
